findings.finding: Scraper SH3 faces the opponent in both slots. Entire crouched body, two independent blades, blade tips, hands and both shoes remain visible. The final combat render and both preserved selection portraits have no opaque background or visible material halo at gameplay scale.

Richard Victim 19 SH4 faces the opponent in both slots. His head, plaid shirt, raised leg, both shoes and curved pipe are complete. His lowest visible shoe pixels remain 8.76 px above the floor, consistent with the intentional slight ghost suspension and anchor y=1. Both preserved selection portraits are complete and clean.

Weeping Bat Downpour faces the opponent in both slots. The head, open mouth, two long arms and claws, two legs and long toes are complete; no wings are added. The actual Canvas combat renders show no gray background rectangle or real alpha halo from hidden RGB. Both preserved selection portraits retain complete fingers and feet.

limits: Actual FightEngine with native Canvas, not browser screenshots. DOM, CSS, browser input, browser decoding and service worker behavior are outside this review.
Static one-frame idle candidates. Introductions, 120 idle updates, rendering and pause do not certify bitmap animation, new attacks or collision timing.
Opposite facing uses the engine mirror. Neither independent rear anatomy nor source fidelity 1:1 is certified.
The three Weeping Bat source pictures are front or three-quarter views; none establishes a true back view. The new lateral pose is a recomposition and its rear details remain unverified.
The four final combat captures and all six preserved selection portrait captures were manually inspected. The four tick0 captures are recorded but are not counted as manual visual inspections.
